column1: # How long each browser suite takes ON THE RUNNER, so `run.js` can pack them into shards.
# A WEIGHT IS A MEASUREMENT WITH A DATE, NEVER A FACT. These decide which shard a suite lands
# in and nothing else: coverage is proven from the receipts each shard writes, so a stale
# weight costs wall clock and cannot cost correctness. That is the only reason this file is
# allowed to exist — it is the one typed list in `app/ui/tests/`, and it is typed because a
# duration is the one thing that cannot be read off disk. Everything a green run DEPENDS on
# MEASURED: run 34448209503, 2026-09-10, `macos-latest`, at 09ada13e — the first green sharded
# pass. Every number is that run's own receipt for that suite, so they come from ONE execution
# and are comparable with each other. Numbers stitched from several sources are not.
#   heaviest suite        305 s (splash.js) — the floor: no shard count gets under it
# THESE REPLACED A LOCAL SET, and the size of the correction is the argument for re-deriving
# them here rather than trusting a laptop. Locally the same 31 suites totalled 756 s and the
# heaviest was `splash.js` at 110 s; on the runner it is 2155 s and 305 s. The RATIOS moved
# too, which is what packing actually depends on: `affordances.js` is 7 percent of the local total
# and 13 percent of the runner's, because runner slowness is not a single constant every suite is
# multiplied by. A packing computed from local seconds is a packing computed from the wrong
# RE-DERIVE THEM THE SAME WAY. Every receipt carries its suite's wall clock, so the current
# numbers are always one command away from the last green run's own log — never a fresh
# stopwatch, and never a mix of the two.
# A suite missing from this file is NOT an error. `run.js` packs it as the heaviest known
# suite and NAMES it in `--plan`, so it lands in the emptiest shard and the assumption is
# visible rather than silent. Adding a suite therefore needs no edit here.
# Longest first, which is also the order the packer walks them in.
